title: Day 5/100 of AI trading $10,000 on Robinhood Agentic
author: Newrateacc
selftext:
Robinhood Portfolio: $10,503.07

Today: down $110.03 (down 1.04%). Red across almost the whole book, the kind of day this series exists to show, not just the good ones.

Worst dollar loser: FAANG+ Momentum, $2,487.66, down $35.81 (down 1.42%). It sold AAPL, AMZN, GOOGL, and NVDA this morning to go all in on META on the daily rerank, then META gave some back into the close.

Worst percent loser: Crypto Rotator, $224.77, down $26.96 (down 10.71%). No trade today, this is just getting hit hard by the crypto crash.

Business As Usual, $2,603.79, down $23.13 (down 0.88%).  
No trade today either, just held plain SPY through a down market, which was exactly how this agent should work.

High Profile Congress, $492.74, down $10.29 (down 2.05%), despite selling IBP and WMT to buy AVUV off a fresh disclosure this morning. Wrong day for it regardless of the trade.

Al Picks & Shovels, $1,042.99, down $7.28 (down 0.69%).  
Another reweight, sold AMD, ANET, DELL, and TSM, bought more NVDA and more SMCI.

Pelosi Tracker, FDA Inspector, Trump Tweet Trader, and The Silicon Overdrive were all down small to medium, single digit to low double digit dollars, nothing broke.

One housekeeping note: The Quality Momentum, the agent I added Monday with $182, got stopped after one day.  
Wanted to try it, decided against keeping it running, so it will not show up in these anymore.

Five days in, this is the worst day of the stretch so far, worse than day 2's small dip. Still up overall since day 1, but days like this are the ones that matter more than the green ones, since anyone can post the good days.

comments.author: leroylabs
comments.body: How will The Quality Momentum's $182 allocation be accounted for after stopping it after one day? With 95 days left, a small “retired agents” row showing its realized P&L, any remaining positions, and where the proceeds went would help keep the experiment interpretable. The screenshot's $10,503.07 gives the account total, but dropping discontinued agents from later breakdowns could make the surviving lineup look stronger even if the total stays accurate. Recording the reason for each retirement would also distinguish discretionary changes from agent failures.
